page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-16 is a virtual machine instance based on AMD EPYC 9J45 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. This flexible compute configuration allocates 1 dedicated physical core presenting 2 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. This yields a memory-dense ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, placing it in a memory-optimized bracket relative to standard compute distributions.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, leaving disk operations to external network-attached block volumes. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware footprint provides high memory capacity relative to its two compute threads, it delivers cost-effective memory capacity without paying for unneeded CPU cores.

Workloads suited for VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-16 include in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, small memory-bound relational or document databases, lightweight application middleware, and background ETL processes that require a larger memory footprint than standard general-purpose profiles provide.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-16 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The configuration provides 1 dedicated physical core executing 2 virtual CPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, delivering an elevated allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server includes no local disk storage and no GPU hardware, relying instead on network block volumes for primary persistence. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external network access. Due to its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is cost-efficient for memory-sensitive environments that do not require high parallel compute capacity. It is primarily suited for small in-memory key-value stores, light transactional databases, data pipeline staging nodes, and low-concurrency application services.
